elements.content: Communication Goal: I can ask for and give directions, talk about transport, check what is possible, and make or change plans.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0-A1 General English
- Unit: Inspired Module 5. Out and About
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Out and About
- Materials: City maps, transport icons, plan cards, voice-note script.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• give simple directions
• compare transport options
• make and change plans politely
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles places, prepositions, and present simple.

Next lesson: Lesson 6 recycles city places to shop, order food, and compare prices.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (15 items):

station — a place where trains or buses stop. Example: The station is near the bank.
supermarket — a large food shop. Example: I buy food at the supermarket.
pharmacy — a shop for medicine. Example: The pharmacy is opposite the bank.
bank — a place for money. Example: Turn left at the bank.
park — a green public space. Example: The park is next to the museum.
museum — a place for art or history. Example: Is there a museum near here?
square — an open public space in a city. Example: The square is in the city centre.
street — a road in a city or town. Example: Go straight along this street.
turn left — to go to the left. Example: Turn left at the bank.
turn right — to go to the right. Example: Turn right at the station.
go straight — to continue forward. Example: Go straight for two blocks.
bus — a large road vehicle for passengers. Example: She goes by bus.
tram — a city vehicle that runs on rails. Example: The tram stops near the market.
train — a vehicle that runs on rails. Example: We take the train at eight.
bike — a bicycle. Example: I go to work by bike.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Go straight and turn left at the station. (giving directions)
• The pharmacy is opposite the supermarket. (describing location)
• How do you get to work? — I usually go by metro. (asking about transport)
• Take the green line and get off at Central. (using public transport)
• Can you pay by card here? — Yes, you can. (checking possibilities)
• Let's meet at seven near the station. (making a plan)
• Sorry, I can't make it on Friday. Can we do Saturday? (changing a plan)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'a place where trains or buses stop'?
Which word means 'a large food shop'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

elements.content: Pronunciation Focus: Direction stress and can/can't weak forms

straight /streɪt/ — long /eɪ/
opposite /ˈɒpəzɪt/ — stress the first syllable
can /kən/ — weak form in sentences
can't /kɑːnt/ — strong form for negatives
Listen and repeat:
Go straight and turn left. The bank is opposite the park. Can you pay by card? No, you can't.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use imperatives to give instructions, directions, and advice.

Form:
Imperatives: Base verb + object: Open the door. Negative: Don't + base verb. Add 'please' to be polite.

Examples:
• Open your book, please.
• Turn left at the bank.
• Don't touch the screen.
• Click the link to order.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
___ the door, please.
___ touch the screen.
___ left at the bank.
___ your name here.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• ... (Open / Close / Click) the ...
• Don't ... (touch / open / click) the ...
• Please ... (turn / go / write) ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• How do you make a cup of tea? Give three instructions.
• How do you get to the station from here?
• What are three classroom instructions?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three instructions for using a phone.
• Write three instructions for making your favourite drink.
Reading: Out and About

Getting to Greenleaf Cafe from Central Station: walk out of the station onto Oak Street. Go straight for two blocks and turn left at the bank. Walk past the pharmacy, and Greenleaf Cafe is on the corner of Oak Street and Park Avenue, opposite the city park. You can sit outside, and you can pay by card or phone. You can't park on Park Avenue during the day, so take the green metro line or walk.
Where is Greenleaf Cafe?
options: on the corner of Oak Street and Park Avenue

elements.content: Can you pay by card?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

Hey Alex, it's Nina. I'm sorry, but I can't make it to the movie at seven. My afternoon meeting is running late. Can we do tomorrow instead? Let's meet at half past six at the Italian place next to the station. Text me if that works for you!
What time is the new plan?
Where is the new meeting place?
options: the Italian place next to the station

elements.content: Speaking task: Use a simple map. Give directions to three places, then compare your commute with your partner.

• How do you get to work or school?
• What is near your home?
• Can you pay by card in your local shops?
• What do you do at the weekend?
• How do you change a plan politely?
Role-play: You are making weekend plans. Suggest an activity, handle one schedule conflict, and agree on a new time and place.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write a short message inviting a friend somewhere. Give two direction steps and say what you can or can't do.
Model: Let's meet at ... Go straight ... Turn left ... I can't ... Can we ...?
